subject: SLA & Support: Aurelia order form — uptime tiers, credits, maintenance splits
messages:
From: Susan Lawson <susan.lawson@aureliahealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Aurelia Health Procurement <procurement@aureliahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Aurelia MSA/Order Form - SLA redlines

Sergio —

Thanks for the draft order form. Attached are Aurelia's initial SLA redlines (see attached Word). High-level items we want on the table: 

• Production uptime: 99.95% (monthly measurement). Non-production: 99.5%.
• Service credits: propose a 3x monthly credit cap for a single month and an annual aggregate cap at 6x the monthly recurring charges; we can discuss phased escalators.
• Response SLAs: P1 = 1 hour (24/7 on-call), P2 = 4 hours (weekday business), P3 = 24 hours. Need confirmation that Redwood on-call covers P1 in-region.
• Maintenance windows: Aurelia prefers weekly 02:00–05:00 local time with no more than four emergency maintenance events per quarter and advance notice of 72 hours for routine maintenance.

Please review and tell us what you can accept vs. what needs redline pushback from legal/ops. Procurement is on copy and will handle the DocuSign route once terms are agreed.

Thanks,
Susan Lawson
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Aurelia Health

Attachments: Aurelia_Redlines_v2.docx (track changes)

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Susan Lawson <susan.lawson@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurelia MSA/Order Form - SLA redlines

Susan —

Appreciate the clear ask and the tracked redlines. Quick read and immediate notes below; Kimberly and Jonas are looped for legal/ops detail.

1) Uptime buckets: Redwood typically guarantees 99.9% for standard production tiers and 99.5% for dev/test. 99.95% is achievable but would map to a higher tier / reserved capacity (Dedicated). If Aurelia needs 99.95 in hosted, we should align on pricing delta or pin usage to Dedicated capacity.

2) Credits: our standard credit framework caps monthly credits at 100% of MRC (1x) and annual at 3x. Moving to 3x monthly / 6x annual materially changes risk profile. We can entertain a phased approach tied to commitment level.

3) Response times: P1 = 1 hour 24/7 is feasible if Aurelia purchases an elevated support plan. Otherwise our standard is P1 = 2 hours.

4) Maintenance windows: weekly 02:00–05:00 local may conflict with our regional maintenance cadence for multi-tenant clusters. We can commit to a consistent weekly window or offer a limited number of maintenance blackout exceptions. Emergency maintenance cap of 4/Q is reasonable but needs definition (what constitutes emergency).

Next steps: Kimberly, can you draft a short counter with acceptable ranges and the pricing deltas for a 99.95 prod SLA and P1 1-hour on-call? Jonas, ops: what constraints for weekly localized windows?

Happy to jump on a 30-min call with Aurelia this week if that helps.

—Sergio
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Susan Lawson <susan.lawson@aureliahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Aug 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurelia MSA/Order Form - SLA redlines

Folks —

Susan, thanks for sending. Per Sergio's note, legal and commercial can propose a middle path that protects both parties. Draft counterpoints below (I'll fold into a tracked doc):

• Uptime: Offer 99.9% hosted production baseline with an optional upgrade to 99.95% via Dedicated reservation. We will include a one-time migration support credit if Aurelia opts to transition to Dedicated within the first 90 days.
• Credits: Counter-proposal: monthly credit cap = 1.5x MRC for the first year, 3x MRC thereafter for customers on a ≥12-month committed Dedicated plan. Annual cap to be set at 3x MRC for hosted customers and 6x for Dedicated with committed term. This can be tied to a minimum ARR threshold.
• Response times: P1 1-hour full 24/7 coverage only for Premier Support add-on. Standard enterprise support remains P1 = 2 hours. We'll state escalation path and contact matrix in the SOW.
• Maintenance: Define "emergency maintenance" as security-critical fixes that cannot be delayed; cap emergency maint to 4/Q and require post-event RCA within 5 business days. For routine maintenance, propose a rolling 03:00–06:00 UTC window for multi-tenant, with the option for Aurelia to request a localized weekly blackout for their Dedicated instances.

I've attached an annotated SLA (Redwood_SLA_annotated.pdf) and will produce a tracked Word to return to Aurelia. If Aurelia pushes 99.95 for hosted, commercial needs to model the uplift; Jonas can feed infra impact.

—Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_annotated.pdf

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Susan Lawson <susan.lawson@aureliahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurelia MSA/Order Form - SLA redlines

Kimberly / Sergio / Susan —

Ops perspective below: 

• 99.95% hosted across multi-tenant clusters is not something we'll promise without capacity reservation. For Dedicated we can guarantee 99.95 with placement and capacity buffers.
• Weekly 02:00–05:00 local windows at scale create coordination complexity (timezones). For hosted, propose a standardized UTC maintenance slot and we will give Aurelia a maintenance calendar 30 days ahead. For Dedicated VPCs we can set a localized weekly window.
• Emergency maint cap (4/Q) is acceptable but we need a clear definition and a runbook insert: vendor-initiated emergency vs. customer-requested emergency.

I will capture the infrastructure and support cost delta and share a short appendix for commercial to include in the order form.

—Jonas Weber
Head of Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Susan Lawson <susan.lawson@aureliahealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Aurelia Health Procurement <procurement@aureliahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurelia MSA/Order Form - SLA redlines

Sergio / Kimberly / Jonas —

Thanks for the rapid turnaround and the detailed counters — those changes are generally acceptable. A few closing asks before we route to procurement/DocuSign: 

• Please insert the Dedicated upgrade option as a clearly priced addendum in the order form so Aurelia can sign the hosted baseline today and add the upgrade within 90 days if we opt to.
• Add the emergency maintenance definition and RCA timing into the SLA body (we need the 5-business-day RCA language).
• Commercial to outline the annual credit cap math in the order form so procurement can sign off quickly.

If you can send an updated tracked order form by EOD Friday (11 Aug) we will target signature next week. Procurement will manage the DocuSign envelope.

Best,
Susan Lawson
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Aurelia Health

Forwarded attachments: Aurelia_Redlines_v2.docx, Redwood_SLA_annotated.pdf
